subject: Stratus Labs — proposed true-up cadence, make-good credits, and invoice line examples
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@stratuslabs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodai.com>
Cc: procure@stratuslabs.com
Date: 2027-10-01T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Question on quarterly true-up + make-good mechanics

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the run-through on Friday. Finance asked me to pull together the outstanding questions so we can get a clean procurement path. A few specific asks: 

1) If we commit to a 12-month tiered commit (e.g., 120M tokens/month committed), how does quarterly true-up work? Do you reconcile only against committed monthly averages or against an annual bucket?
2) In months we underutilize, what form do make-goods take? Credit on the following invoice, or a one-time credit at true-up?
3) If we exceed commit in a month, is overage billed at the standard catalogue per-token rate or a blended rate?

We need a sample invoice line items layout so our AP team can match it to their system. Can you also share any restrictions on rollover or how early termination interacts with unused commit?

Appreciate a concise proposal we can take to procurement.

Best,
Dana Liu
Finance Manager | Stratus Labs
D: +1 415-555-0192

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodai.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on quarterly true-up + make-good mechanics

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, then a short example and the attached workbook (q3-trueup-workbook.xlsx) with calculations you can drop into your procurement template.

Summary proposal (recommended):
- Commit model: 12-month term with monthly committed tokens allocated as a lumped annual bucket for true-up purposes (we reconcile quarterly but measure against the prorated annual commitment to reduce month-to-month noise).
- Quarterly true-up: At each quarter boundary we compare realized usage to the prorated commitment for that quarter. If actual > prorated commitment, excess is billed as an overage at the overage rate (committed discounted rate + fixed delta). If actual < prorated commitment, we create a make-good credit equal to the unused committed portion valued at the committed rate, applied as an invoice credit against the following quarter invoice.
- Make-goods: Credits are issued at the committed (discounted) unit price. Option to apply as a single year-end one-time true-up instead of quarterly credits can be selected in the amendment; default is quarterly credits to speed cashflow neutrality for you.
- Overage billing: Overage is billed at the published overage rate in the amendment (not the on-demand retail rate). For your tier example we propose a 20% delta above the committed unit price for overages within the same tier, and a blended bucket option if you want to smooth spikes across tiers.
- Rollover & termination: Unused monthly tokens do not roll forward beyond the chosen quarter (no multi-quarter rollover). On early termination, unused committed value is treated per the termination clause in the amendment — typically a pro-rata refund credit or accelerated invoice depending on negotiated terms.

Example (numbers pulled into attached workbook):
- Annual commit: 1.44B tokens (120M/month).
- Q1 prorated commit: 360M tokens.
- If Q1 usage = 420M, overage = 60M billed at overage rate (committed unit price * 1.20).
- If Q2 usage = 300M, unused = 60M -> make-good credit = 60M * committed unit price applied against Q3 invoice.

Attached: q3-trueup-workbook.xlsx (breaks down per-month and per-quarter scenarios + sample invoice lines).

Next steps: Ben (cc) will confirm the overage rate roll and Lauren will prepare a short amendment template. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call this week if procurement wants to walk through the workbook.

Thanks,

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Director, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodai.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on quarterly true-up + make-good mechanics

Dana / Tessa —

Couple of operational clarifications from SE perspective: 

- Metering granularity: All token counts are aggregated per customer_id and measured at the invoice boundary. We can surface per-route breakouts in the invoice for Stratus if you need line-level detail for chargeback.
- Blended vs tiered overage: If you expect periodic spikes (bursty ML jobs), we recommend the blended protection add-on in the amendment. That takes spikes under a monthly smoothing policy and bills a blended overage across the quarter to avoid one-time large invoices. I put a worked example tab in the workbook.
- Safeguard: We'll include a soft-notification threshold so your SREs get an alert when trailing 7-day usage hits 85% of monthly commit — gives you time to throttle or request burst credits.

One ask: can we lock the committed unit price for the first 9 months and then allow a single CPI-based adjustment (max +3% y/y) thereafter? That protects your procurement from inflation risk.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@stratuslabs.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-10-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on quarterly true-up + make-good mechanics

Hi all —

Drafted a short amendment (attached: draft-amendment-for-commit.docx) that implements the flow Tessa recommended and the blended/off-ramp options Ben described. Notes: 

- Quarterly true-up clause (Section 2.3) reconciles actual vs prorated quarterly commitment; credits issued within 30 days following quarter close.
- Make-goods are issued as invoice credits at committed price; can elect year-end single true-up instead via checkbox.
- Early termination: refund vs accelerated invoice is negotiable; default is pro-rated refund to minimize surprises for customers.
- Overages: default is per-tier overage multiplier; add-on clause allows blending across tiers for smoothing.

I'll create a DocuSign envelope once we have the final tickbox choices (quarterly credits vs year-end) and the agreed overage delta. Sample invoice lines are included in the amendment appendix.

Link to the HubSpot deal updated here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

--
Lauren Bishop
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question on quarterly true-up + make-good mechanics

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement needed. Quick confirmations before we route for signature: 

- We prefer quarterly credits (not year-end), and we accept the proposed 20% overage delta for same-tier excess.
- Please lock the committed unit price for months 1-9. After month 9, we accept a CPI cap of +3% annually as Ben suggested.
- Can you provide one sample invoice (PDF) showing: committed line, usage line, overage line, and credit application? Our AP needs the naming convention for each line so automation picks it up.

Once we have the sample invoice layout and the DocuSign link, I'll get this routed internally. Procurement will want to see the q3-trueup-workbook.xlsx numbers matched to the invoice.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Dana Liu
Finance Manager | Stratus Labs
procure@stratuslabs.com
